disagreements.about: whether the groove should change when the section does
disagreements.position: a form with one groove for two minutes has no turn
disagreements.settledBy: the form: a section the Peer names as a turn may carry a second groove
disagreements.theirs: a feel is a phrase and one song has one pocket

disagreements.about: whether the break should vary across the form
disagreements.position: the ear wants a turn at the hook
disagreements.settledBy: slice order and chain can change at a turn; the source may not
disagreements.theirs: one bar, rearranged, is the whole craft; a second break is a second source

disagreements.about: whether the bass should change at the hook
disagreements.position: a hook without a lift in the low end is not a hook
disagreements.settledBy: register: the hook may take the line an octave up, not a different line
disagreements.theirs: the line holds the harmony; the hook changes the drums, not the roots

disagreements.about: whether the outside ear outranks the brief
disagreements.position: the listener never reads the brief and only hears the song
disagreements.settledBy: the Peer's readings are heard; the Producer says which change the brief
disagreements.theirs: the brief is the song's; the Peer's ear is a reading, not a ruling

disagreements.about: whether a lift is a layer or a level
disagreements.position: a listener hears a lift as more happening
disagreements.settledBy: both: the Peer counts layers, the Engineer reads the bounce, and the hook needs one of them
disagreements.theirs: a lift is three decibels and a wider top, and no layer is needed

disagreements.about: whether the hook is the words or the section
disagreements.position: the hook is when the song arrives, wherever the title falls
disagreements.settledBy: the title line: if it lands in the section the Peer names, both are right
disagreements.theirs: the hook is the line the listener sings back, and the section is named for it

disagreements.about: whether a progression that never lands is a problem
disagreements.position: a loop that never resolves is the point of this idiom, and the hook does the landing rather than the cadence
disagreements.settledBy: the form: inside a section a loop may hang, at the end of the form something lands
disagreements.theirs: a phrase that never cadences leaves the ear waiting with nothing promised

lineages.instrument: a finished demo, played back as a stranger
lineages.name: Jeff Tweedy
lineages.why: How to Write One Song is a working method for the outside ear turned on your own work: finish the thing before judging it, then listen as someone who has never heard it, and say what you would cut before what you would add. The method is in the book, chapter by chapter, and the Wilco records are the demonstration of cutting the best part when it was in the wrong place.

lineages.name: Nick Cave
lineages.why: The Red Hand Files is years of a songwriter answering, in public and in writing, what a song is doing and whether it works — the outside ear as correspondence, dated and searchable. A lineage that says its readings out loud can be quoted rather than guessed.

lineages.name: Max Martin (as reported)
lineages.why: The method is documented at second hand in enough detail to state as arithmetic: the hook early, the melody as math, the form turning inside a minute, every section earning the next. Reported by Seabrook rather than stated by him, which is why it is the third lineage and every range from it is marked as such.

openQuestions.alternative: In a lo-fi idiom the hook is a texture that is there from the first bar, and the deadline should read the first *change* rather than the first hook — Cave's minute would then be the range, not the exception.

openQuestions.alternative: No: a lineage with no first-person account is folklore, and the ranges should be measured from the records alone and marked inferred.

openQuestions.question: Should a lineage documented only at second hand carry ranges at all?

openQuestions.alternative: Level: a single layer that doubles in loudness is a bigger lift than two quiet ones, and the rule should read the Engineer's bounce when there is one.
